Job Summary: Full-Time Medical Assistant at our Northfield Office. The Medical Assistant is responsible for performing the highest quality of medical, clinical, and clerical tasks in a medical setting. Previous healthcare experience is required.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am - 7:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.<br/> 

Medical Assistant

Job Summary: Full-Time Lead Medical Assistant at our Hillsborough Office. The Lead Medical Assistant provides administrative support to Physicians, Physician Assistants, and Medical Assistants/LPNs by way of supervision and staff development to provide a professional and effective medical operation. Previous healthcare experience is required. Dermatology experience is required.

Schedule:  Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7am-7pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Lead Medical Assistant:

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere that enhances the quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider.
  • Lead by example, maintains office presence and highest level of professionalism.
  • Maintains effective and constructive communication with office management to instill company values, vision, and protocols in all associated colleagues and providers.
  • Have a thorough working knowledge of all standard operating protocol and policies that pertain to the clinical department.
  • Have thorough knowledge of all clinical treatments to appropriately care for the patient’s needs. Proficient in pre-care and post-care treatment instructions. Fully understands provider to patient flow and anticipates provider’s next steps to the best of their ability.
  • Assist the physician in medical, cosmetic, allergy, and/or laser procedures. Preps exam rooms for all procedures and properly cleans exam rooms after every visit.
  • Assist Office Management in successfully running the day-to-day clinical operations of their respective location by providing supervision and evaluation of day-to-day duties.
  • Ensure that all assigned Medical Assistants/LPNs follow company policies and protocols such as adhering to opening and closing checklist are being accounted for daily and properly.
  • On a daily basis, scan all consumables and retail products to assist Office Management with always maintaining an adequate number; when needed, properly place orders via expense protocol for consumables and retail products.
  • Consistently maintain an adequate amount of medical supplies by executing weekly inventory counts, placing bi-weekly medical supply orders along with emergency orders as needed while always considering cost savings measures. Ensures all medical equipment is being properly maintained avoiding running out of key items, overspending or waste.
  • Properly assists provider in recording prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, biopsies, cultures, photos, prescriptions, prior authorization, obtaining consents, and/or procedures within established guidelines.
  • Work with Office Management to audit consumable tracker and laser logs on a weekly basis.
  • Responsible for auditing all specimen logbooks and lab tracker for respective location’s providers. Ensures all books are kept up to date and every provider and MA follow proper protocol.
  • Oversee and ensure all required medical forms (written and/or electric) such as consents, EMR notes, lab results, etc. are organized and submitted with accurate data and in a timely manner.
  • Work closely with management to execute all new protocols and assist with training needs. Works with General/Regional/Clinical Managers to provide onboarding planning, training, and continued education to all new and current assigned Medical Support Staff.
  • Works with MAs, LPNs, and MA Floater to ensure all refill and prior authorization requests in combination with To Do tasks requests to ensure all items are being handled in a timely fashion at respective locations.
  • Assist office management in supervising/finding coverage for necessary shifts should there be a support staff call out, emergency, or PTO taken; steps in and covers shifts on any emergency needs.
  • Must exude a strong understanding of and enforce CLIA, OSHA and HIPAA regulations as well as report and help document any incidents to the respective office management.
  • Properly cross trains to assist in covering the front desk during emergencies, as needed.
  • Must be open to handling any other duties not mentioned above to ensure proper support to the respective office.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

Qualifications:

  • 2 - 3 years of experience working in a dermatology/medical environment preferred.
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems preferred.
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills.
  • Must be professional, reliable, and dedicated employee.
  • Must have strong critical thinking, problem resolution skills and be a great multitasker.
  • Prefer prior experience working in a dermatology / medical environment. 
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends.

Hourly Pay Range: $21.5-27

Job Summary: This role owns growth across both sides of the funnel — acquisition and retention — for our patient base. You’ll dig into our data to uncover new growth opportunities, whether that’s a new channel, an underused segment, or an untapped service line, and you’ll help shape the paid and lifecycle programs that turn those opportunities into results.

Job Responsibilities

  • Lead growth initiatives across the full patient funnel, from acquisition and paid marketing through onboarding, retention, and reactivation.

  • Dive into our patient cohorts to identify untapped segments of value and design corresponding campaigns that drive our highest value segments.

  • Leverage A/B testing and pilot programs to test new tactics, analyze results, and build the business case for those that deserve to scale.

  • Design retention funnels through email, SMS, and other channels that ensure patients stay on schedule, return for follow-up care, and reactivate those at risk of churn

  • Support our cross-sell efforts into cosmetic and allergy services, helping patients discover the full range of care Schweiger offers.

  • Help us think through expansion to additional verticals as Schweiger continues to grow.

  • Use behavioral insights and creative thinking to launch personalized, high-performing campaigns.

  • Design systems using AI to automate the team’s workflow, build dashboards and reports, and extract insights from our data

  • Work directly with operational and clinical stakeholders across our practices to design growth solutions that translate to real impact in our offices

  • Operate comfortably in ambiguity — defining the strategy and structure for new initiatives where there isn’t already a playbook.

  • Continuously test, learn, and iterate, bringing new ideas, channels, and technology to keep Schweiger’s growth engine best-in-class

  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

Qualifications

  • 3-5 years of experience in growth, lifecycle, or performance marketing, ideally in healthcare, healthtech, or other consumer businesses.

  • An analytically minded marketer who is comfortable with data — pulling it, interpreting it, and using it to find and prioritize new growth opportunities.

  • Experience across both retention/lifecycle tools (email, SMS, marketing automation) and paid acquisition channels (Google, Meta, Programmatic, etc.); comfortable moving between the two.

  • Forward thinker in using AI to transform the way they work more efficiently and uncover value within the business

  • Passion for healthcare and the patient experience, with a desire to help build something new at a fast-growing medical group.

  • Working knowledge of HIPAA & OSHA compliance

Compensation Range: $130,000-$150,000

This remote position is open to candidates located in the following states: New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California.

Job Summary: The General Manager oversees its respective centers, teams, and processes that are essential to our success. A General Managers will build a team of capable and competent employees that can enhance and optimize operational performance of their centers.

Job Responsibilities

Develop A-Team that delivers A-Level Operational Outcomes and Processes.

  • Culture of Positivity NPS for providers & staff >82

  • Perform as a stable operations leader – displays strong leadership that achieve KPIs and measurable goals as outlined by the RM team.

  • Optimization of operational processes to deliver on goals – staffing percentages and budget adherence

  • Effective and collaborative management - able to effectively collaborate with other company departments/teams to achieve successful results.

  • Independently drive key change and transformation initiatives aligned with organizational strategic goals

  • Heavy focus on auditing SOPs and accountability of SOP compliance at all respective center levels, as well as supporting providers while coaching and developing staff to ensure all are A players.

  • Hold team accountable for C.A.R.E Core Habits

Specific Goals/Objectives

1. Build a capable and competent Office Team at each office being overseen.

  • Develop the team in a cost-effective manner. Build a knowledge base across all disciplines with cross training employees.

  • Provide a strong culture of continued education and training for all staff members. Manage, develop and coach staff.

  • Strong focus on full accountability of center SOP compliance through consistent auditing and follow through at offices.

2. Achieve monthly center goals set forth by the GM Report and KPIs.

  • Track to financial goals and patient satisfaction goals which will be updated ad outlined by the operations team and shared with GMs monthly at a minimum unless the GMs are made aware of any delays.

  • Ensure Staffing, Medical Supplies and Office Supplies are beneath guidance figures noted below

3. Promote a culture of positivity and help build a company that has long-term sustainability.

4. Obtain high levels of patient satisfaction.

  • Goal is a net promoter score above 82%

  • All patient messages resolved within 24hrs, and patient updated daily until resolved

  • Continued 4/5 Star external reviews

5. Achieve smooth running office level operations and site level autonomy.

  • Frequent check in with providers via call, meetings for two way and consistent communication

  • Minimal provider and staff complaints

  • Offices should be able to run autonomously daily with majority of problems resolved independently without GM presence

  • Create a positive and respectful center environment.

  • All audit logs (labs, RX, open notes, messages, Klara inbox, tasking) completed end of day at each office

  • Cross training of staff for versatile staffing

  • Monthly staff meetings recommended

  • Inventory and Cash management as per SOP guidelines

  • Scheduled on site visits for preparation in time spent in each office and allowing staff and providers to prepare

  • First line of contact for all front desk and MA issues always

  • Ensure that all offices appointments for 2 days ahead are checked for accuracy and corrected if inaccurately scheduled.

  • Collaboration with PSC on office updates, provider updates and anything anyone scheduling would need to know

  • Take responsibility when office team makes mistakes in coaching and learning sessions

  • For an office that has MOHs- MOHs cases are done in house through provider-provider referrals unless the MOHs surgeon or patient have requested otherwise, CLIA certification and lab directorship is up to date and maintained. Mohs staff is properly credentialed and trained.

    • Post care concerned for MOHs are set up to go directly to the surgeon

    • GM is responsible for knowledge of CLIA needs and works with lab to make sure up to date information

6. Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

KPIs: To be discussed based on role and updated annually.

Qualifications

  • 2 or more years of leadership experience preferred

  • Healthcare administration or management background preferred

  • Strong computer literacy

  • Leadership qualities with good communication skills

  • Conflict resolution skills must be developed

  • Dermatology experience preferred

  • Working knowledge of HIPAA & OSHA compliance

Competencies

  • Knowledge and Proactive Critical Thinking – Initiates to have advanced level knowledge of all company systems such as Nextech, Patient Acquisition, Klara, iPad, General and Cosmetic Dermatology and inter-center communication tools to achieve high level day to day operational results.

  • Leadership and Growth Oriented – Experienced and processes orientated high growth leader with track record for finding innovative ways to grow revenue and increase margins

  • Strategic and Efficient Planning - Prepares for what is ahead with a focus on data, details, and analysis. Able to execute efficiently and thoughtful with minimal wasted/prolonged timing.

  • Honesty/integrity/culture inspiring – Earns trust with staff, providers and patients and maintains confidence. Deliver message with a kind, empathic, firm but direct and honest way.

  • Talent Appreciation - inspires, motivates, coaches, and develops others. Listens well and continuously learns and seeks advice and feedback from others - team Builder, leader, and manager – creates a culture of positivity

  • Effective Communicator - Communicates passionately, effectively, and persuasively across a diverse set of stakeholders. Able to create processes and structures to facilitate effective communication both internally and externally. Demonstrates an ability to manage conflict, build consensus, and facilitate problem-solving.

  • Organized Planning and Results Oriented - relentlessly pursues ongoing improvement and results. Flexible, with a strong work ethic and an entrepreneurial spirit to accommodate high level of responsibility and multiple priorities. Creates a culture of mutual accountability. Job Summary: Full-Time Medical Coordinator at our Northfield Office. The Medical Coordinator role supports clinical and administrative duties, with a focus on both Medical Assistant and Patient Coordinator functions. This role is responsible for performing the highest quality of clinical and front office responsibilities to support patients and providers. Previous healthcare experience is required.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am - 7:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Medical Coordinator (Medical Assistant/ Patient Coordinator)

  • Patient and Provider Support: Foster a welcoming and professional environment to enhance patient care and support the provider. Maintain a consistent and professional office presence.
  • Clinical Assistance: Assist providers with medical, cosmetic, and laser procedures. Ensure proficiency in all treatments, as well as pre-care and post-care instructions, anticipating provider needs to optimize patient flow.
  • Operational Duties: Prepare and maintain exam rooms before and after procedures. Ensure equipment is in working order and perform daily inventory checks on supplies, including retail and cosmetic products. Alert the team and General Manager of any low supplies as needed.
  • Inventory Management: Oversee the stocking of medical supplies and equipment. Ensure that all supplies are adequately stocked and maintain inventory records as requested.
  • Documentation and Patient Management: Properly document prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, biopsies, cultures, photos, and patient consent forms. Manage follow-up appointments and track inventory used during each visit.
  • Patient Interaction: Take payments, manage patient scheduling, and ensure proper documentation of insurance cards, referrals, and demographic information. Uphold privacy standards, ensuring sensitive information is handled securely, per HIPAA regulations.
  • Financial Responsibilities: Complete daily financial tasks, including accurate cash handling, entering charges and payments, and ensuring cash is properly accounted for at the end of each shift. Handle petty cash and deposit all collected payments securely.
  • Phone and Communication Management: Answer all phone calls promptly, confirm Zocdoc appointments, and make outgoing calls for patient retention. Maintain an organized and neat work area, ensuring patient privacy is preserved.
  • Administrative Duties: Ensure that patient records are created and maintained accurately. Check emails and scan inboxes regularly to address time-sensitive issues. Perform other duties as assigned by supervisors.

Qualifications

  • 6 months to 1 year of experience in a dermatology or medical environment preferred.
  • Proficiency in EMR systems and patient scheduling tools preferred.
  • High School Diploma or GED required; advanced education is encouraged.
  • Certification as a Medical Assistant is highly encouraged.
  • Must be proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Professional, reliable, and dedicated to maintaining high-quality service standards.
  • Must be familiar with HIPAA and OSHA compliance.
  • Work Environment: This role is primarily office-based, utilizing standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and fax machines.

Hourly Pay Range: $18 - $22

job.title: Director – Specialty Operations
job.description:
Schweiger is one of the leading dermatology practices in the country with over 580+ healthcare providers and over 170+ offices in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California. Schweiger provides medical, cosmetic, and surgical dermatology and allergy services with over 2.5 million patient visits annually.<br/><br/>Our mission is to create the Ultimate Patient Experience and a great working environment for our providers, support staff and all team members.<br/><br/>Schweiger has been included in the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies in America list for seven consecutive years. Schweiger has also received Great Place to Work certification. To learn more, click here.

<br/>

Schweiger's Ultimate Employee Experience:  

  • Positive work environment with the tools to need to do your job and grow
  • Full time employees (30+ hours per week) are eligible for:
    • Medical (Virtual Care included), HSA/FSA, Dental, Vision on 1st of the month after hire date
    • 401K after 30 days of employment
    • Company Sponsored Short Term Disability (Only applicable for non-California employee)
    • Pre-tax savings available for public transit commuters
    • Your birthday is an additional personal holiday
  • Part-time employees (less than 30 hours) are eligible for:
    • Dental and Vision on 1st of the month after date of hire
    • 401K after 30 days of employment
  • Employee discounts on Schweiger skin care products & cosmetic services 
<br/>

Position Summary

The Director of Specialty Operations serves as the operational leader for an assigned clinical specialty within Schweiger’s multi-state platform, and as the enterprise subject matter expert on how that specialty operates. The position is accountable for the specialty's performance, including budget, expense, revenue, provider productivity, and recruitment objectives, and for building the organizational capability required to operate and scale that specialty across the clinic network.

The work of the specialty is performed in the clinics by teams that do not report to this position. The Director therefore achieves the specialty's objectives through structured cross-functional partnership and through the development of the field leaders who own day to day execution. The Director advocates for the specialty across the enterprise, ensures each supporting function has what it needs to serve the specialty, and ensures the specialty's requirements are reflected in enterprise processes as those processes evolve.

Assignments are portable by design. The Director leads a specialty through its build, development, and integration phases until it reaches operational maturity, at which point the assignment transitions to the next specialty priority.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Specialty Performance and Accountability

  • Hold accountability for the assigned specialty's budget, expense, revenue, and productivity targets.

  • Own specialty metrics and P&L reporting in partnership with the Sr. Vice President, and establish consistent, repeatable reporting standards.

  • Identify performance variances by region, office, and provider, and drive corrective action through the appropriate operational owners.

  • Define the specialty's operating standards and the criteria for successful performance at the clinic level.

Field Leadership Capability (Primary Objective)

  • Develop General Managers and Regional Managers to a level of specialty acumen that allows them to lead the specialty independently within their clinics and regions.

  • Partner with clinical leadership, training, and operations to build the specialty's education curriculum, standard operating procedures, and reference materials, and to design how that content is delivered, reinforced, and retained. Adoption in the field, rather than availability of material, is the measure.

  • Establish the benchmark and measurement standard for field acumen in partnership with the Operations Vice Presidents, and report against it.

  • Serve as the development and escalation resource for General Managers and Regional Managers.

Subject Matter Expertise

The Director is the designated operational subject matter expert for the assigned specialty. Clinical direction and standards of care remain with clinical leadership. The Director partners with clinical leaders and is responsible for translating clinical requirements into an operating model the organization can execute, support, and scale.

  • Maintain expert-level command of the specialty's operating model, workflow, staffing model, supply chain, documentation and coding requirements, regulatory obligations, and growth levers.

  • Partner with clinical leadership on protocols, quality standards, and provider-facing guidance, and ensure the operational design supports them.

  • Serve as the assigned SME to the integration team, the workflow development team, and any enterprise initiative that touches the specialty.

  • Translate specialty requirements into language and specifications that non-specialty functions can act on.

  • Advise executive leadership on specialty strategy, investment, and operational risk.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Advocacy

Building and scaling a specialty is a shared effort. The Director is responsible for ensuring that effort is coordinated, that each function understands what the specialty requires of it, and that capability is built in partnership rather than in isolation. Core partnerships include:

  • Clinical Leadership. Partner with specialty and enterprise clinical leadership on protocols, quality standards, provider onboarding, and scope of practice, and ensure the operating model reflects clinical direction as it evolves.

  • Integration. Partner with the integration team, which ultimately owns the integration of newly hired providers (if necessary) and acquired practices, to ensure specialty requirements are built into the standard integration model and applied consistently as the organization grows.

  • Finance. Partner on the financial infrastructure the specialty requires, including accounts payable workflows, cost and inventory treatment, capital requests, and specialty-level financial reporting, and support the evolution of those processes as the specialty scales.

  • Revenue Cycle Management. Partner on coding, charge capture, payer policy, prior authorization, and denial trends specific to the specialty, and ensure billing practices keep pace with changes in the service model.

  • Marketing. Partner on brand positioning, patient acquisition, and provider utilization for the specialty, including how a newly built specialty is introduced to patients and referral sources.

  • Training and Learning. Partner on curriculum design, delivery, and competency validation for clinical and non-clinical staff.

  • Talent Acquisition. Define the provider profile, target markets, and pipeline requirements for the specialty, and partner to achieve headcount and recruitment goals. The Director defines what the organization is recruiting for.

  • Business Development. Support diligence and evaluation on acquisitions and partnerships involving the specialty.

  • Legal, Compliance, and Quality. Partner to identify the regulatory, accreditation, licensure, and clinical governance requirements that apply to the specialty, and to build the controls, documentation, and monitoring needed to meet them as the specialty scales.

  • Information Technology and Clinical Systems. Partner on EMR configuration, reporting infrastructure, and technology needed to support specialty workflows.

Service Line Development

  • Scope, build, and launch new services within the assigned specialty.

  • Build the operating documentation the specialty requires, including standard operating procedures, workflows, and role definitions, in partnership with the functions that own them.

  • Define the specialty's growth roadmap and the operational requirements needed to support it.

  • Evolve specialty workflows where performance, compliance, or scale requires it, prioritizing based on impact.

Centralized Specialty Operations

  • Lead the centralized teams and programs required by the assigned specialty, which may include laboratory operations, coordinator programs, or similar functions. These functions follow the assignment rather than the individual.

  • As/if needed, build and execute the transition plan that moves those centralized functions to their permanent organizational home as the specialty reaches maturity.

Scope and Authority

This position carries accountability for specialty outcomes without direct authority over the clinic teams that execute the work. Clinics escalate to their General Manager. General Managers and Regional Managers partner with this position. Preserving that structure is part of the role, as the objective is to build durable capability in the field rather than to create a permanent central dependency.

Success in this position requires influence, credibility, and disciplined partnership across functions. A candidate who relies on positional authority to drive change within a distributed field organization is unlikely to succeed in this seat.

Initial Assignment

The first assignment is the allergy specialty, which is established and performing and now moving from its build phase into deeper integration across the organization. The focus is embedding the specialty into everyday field operations so that General Managers and Regional Managers lead it as part of their core business.

Objectives for the first twelve to eighteen months:

  • Measurable improvement in General Manager and Regional Manager allergy acumen against a defined benchmark.

  • Allergy provider headcount and recruitment objectives met.

  • Biologics service line launched, with asthma scoped for the following phase.

  • Transition plan for the compounding laboratory built and the handoff completed.

  • Consistent, reliable reporting on allergy P&L and specialty metrics established.

Upon reaching those objectives, the assignment shifts to the next specialty priority as determined by the Sr. Vice President.

Qualifications

This position calls for operational strength first. Schweiger is looking for candidates who are comfortable working at both the strategic and the execution level, and who have helped define what gets built rather than only carrying out a plan handed to them. Clinical or specialty experience is valuable and preferred, but it is not required. Candidates without a clinical background will be evaluated on the strength of their operating track record.

Required

  • Progressive experience in multi-site healthcare operations, service line management, or a comparable operating role at director-level scope.

  • Demonstrated ability to work across strategy and execution, shaping what gets built and then running the work to completion.

  • Experience defining scope in ambiguous conditions, where the operating model, standards, and measures did not yet exist.

  • Demonstrated accountability for a budget or P&L, with the ability to speak to operating levers rather than reporting alone.

  • Demonstrated success building capability within a distributed field organization, including developing leaders who do not report to the position.

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and deliver results through teams outside of direct reporting authority.

  • Ability to draw expertise from clinical and functional leaders and convert it into an operating model, documentation, and training the organization can use.

  • Analytical fluency sufficient to build and maintain performance reporting, not solely to interpret it.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate specialty detail for executive, clinical, and operational audiences.

  • Ability to travel regularly across the SDG footprint.

Preferred

  • Experience launching or scaling a service line within a multi-site provider organization.

  • Experience supporting practice acquisitions or provider integration.

  • Clinical background, or direct experience working within a clinical specialty.

Compensation: $100,000-$140,000

This remote position is open to candidates located in the following states: New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California

Job Summary: Full-Time Lead Medical Assistant at our Princeton and Somerset Offices. The Lead Medical Assistant provides administrative support to Physicians, Physician Assistants, and Medical Assistants/LPNs by way of supervision and staff development to provide a professional and effective medical operation. Previous healthcare experience is required. Dermatology experience is required.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am - 7:00pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Lead Medical Assistant:

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere that enhances the quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider.
  • Lead by example, maintains office presence and highest level of professionalism.
  • Maintains effective and constructive communication with office management to instill company values, vision, and protocols in all associated colleagues and providers.
  • Have a thorough working knowledge of all standard operating protocol and policies that pertain to the clinical department.
  • Have thorough knowledge of all clinical treatments to appropriately care for the patient’s needs. Proficient in pre-care and post-care treatment instructions. Fully understands provider to patient flow and anticipates provider’s next steps to the best of their ability.
  • Assist the physician in medical, cosmetic, allergy, and/or laser procedures. Preps exam rooms for all procedures and properly cleans exam rooms after every visit.
  • Assist Office Management in successfully running the day-to-day clinical operations of their respective location by providing supervision and evaluation of day-to-day duties.
  • Ensure that all assigned Medical Assistants/LPNs follow company policies and protocols such as adhering to opening and closing checklist are being accounted for daily and properly.
  • On a daily basis, scan all consumables and retail products to assist Office Management with always maintaining an adequate number; when needed, properly place orders via expense protocol for consumables and retail products.
  • Consistently maintain an adequate amount of medical supplies by executing weekly inventory counts, placing bi-weekly medical supply orders along with emergency orders as needed while always considering cost savings measures. Ensures all medical equipment is being properly maintained avoiding running out of key items, overspending or waste.
  • Properly assists provider in recording prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, biopsies, cultures, photos, prescriptions, prior authorization, obtaining consents, and/or procedures within established guidelines.
  • Work with Office Management to audit consumable tracker and laser logs on a weekly basis.
  • Responsible for auditing all specimen logbooks and lab tracker for respective location’s providers. Ensures all books are kept up to date and every provider and MA follow proper protocol.
  • Oversee and ensure all required medical forms (written and/or electric) such as consents, EMR notes, lab results, etc. are organized and submitted with accurate data and in a timely manner.
  • Work closely with management to execute all new protocols and assist with training needs. Works with General/Regional/Clinical Managers to provide onboarding planning, training, and continued education to all new and current assigned Medical Support Staff.
  • Works with MAs, LPNs, and MA Floater to ensure all refill and prior authorization requests in combination with To Do tasks requests to ensure all items are being handled in a timely fashion at respective locations.
  • Assist office management in supervising/finding coverage for necessary shifts should there be a support staff call out, emergency, or PTO taken; steps in and covers shifts on any emergency needs.
  • Must exude a strong understanding of and enforce CLIA, OSHA and HIPAA regulations as well as report and help document any incidents to the respective office management.
  • Properly cross trains to assist in covering the front desk during emergencies, as needed.
  • Must be open to handling any other duties not mentioned above to ensure proper support to the respective office.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

Qualifications:

  • 2 - 3 years of experience working in a dermatology/medical environment required.
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems preferred.
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills.
  • Must be professional, reliable, and dedicated employee.
  • Must have strong critical thinking, problem resolution skills and be a great multitasker.
  • Prefer prior experience working in a dermatology / medical environment. 
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends.

Hourly Pay Range: $20 - $25

Job Summary: The General Manager oversees its respective centers, teams, and processes that are essential to our success. A General Managers will build a team of capable and competent employees that can enhance and optimize operational performance of their centers.

Job Responsibilities

Develop A-Team that delivers A-Level Operational Outcomes and Processes.

  • Culture of Positivity NPS for providers & staff >82
  • Perform as a stable operations leader – displays strong leadership that achieve KPIs and measurable goals as outlined by the RM team.
  • Optimization of operational processes to deliver on goals – staffing percentages and budget adherence
  • Effective and collaborative management - able to effectively collaborate with other company departments/teams to achieve successful results.
  • Independently drive key change and transformation initiatives aligned with organizational strategic goals
  • Heavy focus on auditing SOPs and accountability of SOP compliance at all respective center levels, as well as supporting providers while coaching and developing staff to ensure all are A players.
  • Hold team accountable for C.A.R.E Core Habits

Specific Goals/Objectives

1. Build a capable and competent Office Team at each office being overseen.

  • Develop the team in a cost-effective manner. Build a knowledge base across all disciplines with cross training employees.
  • Provide a strong culture of continued education and training for all staff members. Manage, develop and coach staff.
  • Strong focus on full accountability of center SOP compliance through consistent auditing and follow through at offices.

2. Achieve monthly center goals set forth by the GM Report and KPIs.

  • Track to financial goals and patient satisfaction goals which will be updated ad outlined by the operations team and shared with GMs monthly at a minimum unless the GMs are made aware of any delays.
  • Ensure Staffing, Medical Supplies and Office Supplies are beneath guidance figures noted below

3. Promote a culture of positivity and help build a company that has long-term sustainability.

4. Obtain high levels of patient satisfaction.

  • Goal is a net promoter score above 82%
  • All patient messages resolved within 24hrs, and patient updated daily until resolved
  • Continued 4/5 Star external reviews

5. Achieve smooth running office level operations and site level autonomy.

  • Frequent check in with providers via call, meetings for two way and consistent communication
  • Minimal provider and staff complaints
  • Offices should be able to run autonomously daily with majority of problems resolved independently without GM presence
  • Create a positive and respectful center environment.
  • All audit logs (labs, RX, open notes, messages, Klara inbox, tasking) completed end of day at each office
  • Cross training of staff for versatile staffing
  • Monthly staff meetings recommended
  • Inventory and Cash management as per SOP guidelines
  • Scheduled on site visits for preparation in time spent in each office and allowing staff and providers to prepare
  • First line of contact for all front desk and MA issues always
  • Ensure that all offices appointments for 2 days ahead are checked for accuracy and corrected if inaccurately scheduled.
  • Collaboration with PSC on office updates, provider updates and anything anyone scheduling would need to know
  • Take responsibility when office team makes mistakes in coaching and learning sessions
  • For an office that has MOHs- MOHs cases are done in house through provider-provider referrals unless the MOHs surgeon or patient have requested otherwise, CLIA certification and lab directorship is up to date and maintained. Mohs staff is properly credentialed and trained.
    • Post care concerned for MOHs are set up to go directly to the surgeon
    • GM is responsible for knowledge of CLIA needs and works with lab to make sure up to date information

6. Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

KPIs: To be discussed based on role and updated annually.

Qualifications

  • 2 or more years of leadership experience preferred
  • Healthcare administration or management background preferred
  • Strong computer literacy
  • Leadership qualities with good communication skills
  • Conflict resolution skills must be developed
  • Dermatology experience preferred
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA & OSHA compliance

Competencies

  • Knowledge and Proactive Critical Thinking – Initiates to have advanced level knowledge of all company systems such as Nextech, Patient Acquisition, Klara, iPad, General and Cosmetic Dermatology and inter-center communication tools to achieve high level day to day operational results.
  • Leadership and Growth Oriented – Experienced and processes orientated high growth leader with track record for finding innovative ways to grow revenue and increase margins
  • Strategic and Efficient Planning - Prepares for what is ahead with a focus on data, details, and analysis. Able to execute efficiently and thoughtful with minimal wasted/prolonged timing.
  • Honesty/integrity/culture inspiring – Earns trust with staff, providers and patients and maintains confidence. Deliver message with a kind, empathic, firm but direct and honest way.
  • Talent Appreciation - inspires, motivates, coaches, and develops others. Listens well and continuously learns and seeks advice and feedback from others - team Builder, leader, and manager – creates a culture of positivity
  • Effective Communicator - Communicates passionately, effectively, and persuasively across a diverse set of stakeholders. Able to create processes and structures to facilitate effective communication both internally and externally. Demonstrates an ability to manage conflict, build consensus, and facilitate problem-solving.
  • Organized Planning and Results Oriented - relentlessly pursues ongoing improvement and results. Flexible, with a strong work ethic and an entrepreneurial spirit to accommodate high level of responsibility and multiple priorities. Creates a culture of mutual accountability. Plans, organizes, schedules and budgets in an efficient, productive manger. Focuses on key priorities.

Travel

Employee is expected to be in their office(s) during the week. Other travel outside of their region and/or to the corporate office may be needed from time to time.

Compensation Range: $65,000 - $73,000

Job Summary: Full-Time Lead Medical Assistant at our Hoboken, NJ Office. The Lead Medical Assistant provides administrative support to Physicians, Physician Assistants, and Medical Assistants/LPNs by way of supervision and staff development to provide a professional and effective medical operation. Previous healthcare experience is required. Dermatology experience is required.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7am to 7pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Lead Medical Assistant:

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere that enhances the quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider.
  • Lead by example, maintains office presence and highest level of professionalism.
  • Maintains effective and constructive communication with office management to instill company values, vision, and protocols in all associated colleagues and providers.
  • Have a thorough working knowledge of all standard operating protocol and policies that pertain to the clinical department.
  • Have thorough knowledge of all clinical treatments to appropriately care for the patient’s needs. Proficient in pre-care and post-care treatment instructions. Fully understands provider to patient flow and anticipates provider’s next steps to the best of their ability.
  • Assist the physician in medical, cosmetic, allergy, and/or laser procedures. Preps exam rooms for all procedures and properly cleans exam rooms after every visit.
  • Assist Office Management in successfully running the day-to-day clinical operations of their respective location by providing supervision and evaluation of day-to-day duties.
  • Ensure that all assigned Medical Assistants/LPNs follow company policies and protocols such as adhering to opening and closing checklist are being accounted for daily and properly.
  • On a daily basis, scan all consumables and retail products to assist Office Management with always maintaining an adequate number; when needed, properly place orders via expense protocol for consumables and retail products.
  • Consistently maintain an adequate amount of medical supplies by executing weekly inventory counts, placing bi-weekly medical supply orders along with emergency orders as needed while always considering cost savings measures. Ensures all medical equipment is being properly maintained avoiding running out of key items, overspending or waste.
  • Properly assists provider in recording prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, biopsies, cultures, photos, prescriptions, prior authorization, obtaining consents, and/or procedures within established guidelines.
  • Work with Office Management to audit consumable tracker and laser logs on a weekly basis.
  • Responsible for auditing all specimen logbooks and lab tracker for respective location’s providers. Ensures all books are kept up to date and every provider and MA follow proper protocol.
  • Oversee and ensure all required medical forms (written and/or electric) such as consents, EMR notes, lab results, etc. are organized and submitted with accurate data and in a timely manner.
  • Work closely with management to execute all new protocols and assist with training needs. Works with General/Regional/Clinical Managers to provide onboarding planning, training, and continued education to all new and current assigned Medical Support Staff.
  • Works with MAs, LPNs, and MA Floater to ensure all refill and prior authorization requests in combination with To Do tasks requests to ensure all items are being handled in a timely fashion at respective locations.
  • Assist office management in supervising/finding coverage for necessary shifts should there be a support staff call out, emergency, or PTO taken; steps in and covers shifts on any emergency needs.
  • Must exude a strong understanding of and enforce CLIA, OSHA and HIPAA regulations as well as report and help document any incidents to the respective office management.
  • Properly cross trains to assist in covering the front desk during emergencies, as needed.
  • Must be open to handling any other duties not mentioned above to ensure proper support to the respective office.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

Qualifications:

  • 2 - 3 years of experience working in a dermatology/medical environment preferred.
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems preferred.
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills.
  • Must be professional, reliable, and dedicated employee.
  • Must have strong critical thinking, problem resolution skills and be a great multitasker.
  • Prefer prior experience working in a dermatology / medical environment. 
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends.

Hourly Pay Range: $21.5- $27

Job Summary: Full Time Assistant General Manager position at our Boca Raton, FL Office. The Assistant General Manager oversees its respective office, teams, and processes that are essential to our success. An AGM will help build a team of capable and competent employees that can enhance and optimize operational performance of their office.<br/><br/>Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with occasional Saturdays during business hours of 6am-6pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Job Responsibilities

  • Develop A-Team that delivers A-Level Operational Outcomes and Processes

  • Culture of Positivity NPS for providers & staff >82

  • Perform as a stable operations leader – displays strong leadership that achieve KPIs and measurable goals such as financial collections, no show rates, provider utilization, etc.

  • Optimization of operational processes to deliver on goals – staffing percentages and budget adherence

  • Effective and collaborative management – able to effectively collaborate with other company departments/teams to achieve successful results

  • Independently drive key change and transformation initiatives aligned with organizational strategic goals

  • Heavy focus on auditing SOPs and accountability of SOP compliance at all respective office levels, as well as supporting providers while coaching and developing staff to ensure all are A players

  • Hold team accountable for C.A.R.E Core Habits

Specific Goals/Objectives

1. Build a capable and competent Office Team while working closely with Operations Departments, HR, Billing, Accounting, IT, Marketing, PSC, respective providers, and fellow offices.

  • Develop the office team in a cost-effective manner. Build a knowledge base across all disciplines

  • Provide a strong culture of continued education and training for all staff members. Assist in managing, developing and coaching PCs and MAs

  • Strong focus on full accountability of office SOP compliance through consistent auditing and follow through at office level

2. Achieve monthly office goals set forth by the GM Report and KPIs.

  • Track to financial goals and patient satisfaction goals, including but not exclusively: no show rates, financial balance collection, inventory tracking, auditing check in and check out procedures, patient satisfaction, follow up rates, etc.

  • Ensure Staffing, Medical Supplies and Office Supplies are meeting or below plan

3. Promote a culture of positivity and help build a company that has long-term sustainability.

4.Obtain high levels of patient satisfaction.

  • Goal is a net promoter score above 82 or office specific goal

  • NPS results are reviewed daily and responded to as needed for promoter and detractor scores

  • NPS themes per office and provider team are reviewed and action plans put in place as needed to address areas of opportunity

  • All patient messages resolved within 24hrs and patient updated daily until resolved

  • 15 4/5 Star external reviews (Yelp/Google)

5. Achieve smooth running office level operations and site level autonomy.

  • Minimal provider and staff complaints

  • Office should be able to run autonomously daily with majority of problems resolved independently

  • Create a positive and respectful office environment

  • All biopsies or labs from over two weeks ago closed out and acted upon

  • Collection reconciled and deposits managed per SOP

  • Understand MA and PC role sufficient to fill in as needed

  • Regular communication with provider and involvement in office decision to ensure team alignment

  • Ensure that all office appointments for 2 days ahead are checked for accuracy and corrected if inaccurately scheduled

  • Assist in staff scheduling management and provider scheduling data entry for payroll

Job Summary: A Regional Manager (RM) is responsible for full regional performance across multiple practices. This role owns regional P&L results, drives strategic growth, develops high-performing leadership teams, and ensures consistent execution of The Schweiger Way.

Job Responsibilities

1. Regional P&L Ownership & Financial Performance

  • Own full regional P&L performance, including revenue growth, expense management, margin optimization, and EBITDA contribution.
  • Lead and hold General Managers (GMs) and Practice Managers (PMs) accountable for achieving monthly and annual financial targets and key performance indicators.
  • Analyze regional performance trends, identify risks and opportunities, and implement data-driven action plans to drive measurable improvement.
  • Present monthly regional performance insights, forecasts, and strategic initiatives to the Leadership Team.

2. Strategic Growth & Market Expansion

  • Lead regional growth initiatives, including de novo launches, acquisition integrations, provider ramp-up strategies, and capacity planning.
  • Optimize provider scheduling and utilization to increase access, enhance productivity, and maximize revenue.
  • Identify and execute market expansion and service line growth opportunities within the region.
  • Partner cross-functionally to ensure successful integration of new offices, providers, and operational initiatives.

3. Provider Engagement & Retention

  • Partner with the Regional Medical Director to proactively manage provider engagement, satisfaction, and retention.
  • Identify providers at risk and implement structured action plans to address concerns and improve experience.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, and seamless integration of new providers to ensure strong ramp-up and long-term success.
  • Maintain a high-performing provider environment aligned with the company’s clinical and cultural standards.

4. Leadership Development & Talent Strategy

  • Build and develop a high-performing leadership bench through structured coaching, succession planning, and performance management of GMs and PMs.
  • Evaluate leadership capabilities and make strategic talent decisions to meet evolving business needs.
  • Foster accountability, ownership, and operational excellence across all offices.
  • Promote a culture of positivity and engagement, maintaining provider and staff Net Promoter Scores.

5. Operational Excellence & Compliance

  • Ensure consistent execution of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) through structured audits, performance oversight, and accountability frameworks.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, patient flow, and service excellence.
  • Oversee resolution of escalated patient concerns in partnership with the Regional Medical Director and local leadership to protect patient experience and brand reputation.
  • Ensure regional compliance with HIPAA, OSHA, CLIA (when applicable) and all regulatory requirements through proactive oversight and corrective action planning.

6. Enterprise Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as the primary operational liaison between regional offices and corporate departments.
  • Lead regional implementation of company-wide strategic initiatives and transformation efforts.
  • Model and champion The Schweiger Way fundamentals to foster a consistent, positive, and high-performing culture.

7. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Responsible for delivering measurable regional results aligned to annually established KPIs by Operations Leadership.
  • Sets clear expectations with direct reports, monitors performance through data dashboards and business reviews, and ensures consistent execution of company initiatives to achieve financial, operational, and cultural targets.

Qualifications

  • 5 or more years of leadership required.
  • Healthcare administration or management background.
  • Conflict resolution skills must be exceptionally developed.
  • Leadership qualities with excellent communication skills.
  • Strong computer literacy.
  • Dermatology and/or Allergy experience preferred.

Travel

Employee is expected to travel to offices within their region throughout the week to complete site visits and meet with Providers, GM / RM, and office teams. About 80% of the RMs weekly time should be spent on site at offices. Other travel outside of their region and/or to the corporate office may be needed from time to time.

Work Environment

  • This job description indicates in general the nature and levels of work, knowledge, skills, abilities, and other essential functions (as covered under the Americans with Disabilities Act) expected of an employee.
  • This job operates in a professional work environment.
  • This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, telephones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, and fax machines.
  • While performing the duties of this job, employee is regularly required to talk; hear; stand; walk; use hands to finger; handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms.

Compensation: $105,000 - $125,000

Job Summary: Full-Time Clinical Research Coordinator in our Verona Office. The Clinical Research Coordinator will support the daily management of clinical research protocols, ensuring maximum study documentation, quality assurance, electronic data entry, subject recruitment, subject management, CRF/eCRF completion, completion of source documents, conflict resolution, study training, and attending research meetings.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7am-7:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Job Description

Clinical Research Coordinator

  • Attend investigator meetings as required. Some travel necessary/required.

  • Assure patients are scheduled and seen according to protocol requirements. 

  • Monitor patient visits and progress throughout the study and routinely inform the principle investigator(s) of patient study status and new updates. ​

  • Document date drug/devices and supplies received​

  • Prepare subject files

  • Multitask between multiple projects and offices and follow through with all ongoing tasks and/or office needs. 

  • Recruitment of patients for randomization into studies. 

  • Assist in any special projects Operations Team needs assistance with.

Qualifications

  • phlebotomy experience required

Job Summary: Part-Time Patient Coordinator at our West Orange, NJ Office. The Patient Coordinator executes all front office duties and provides support to patients, providers, and support staff. Previous healthcare experience is required. Open to no experience but has an interest in healthcare, teamwork experience, and detail oriented with a flexible schedule.

Schedule:  Part-Time, less than 30 hours per week. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7am-7pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Patient Coordinator/Medical Receptionist:

  • Proficiently and efficiently handle all incoming phone calls, scheduling-related tasks and online leads in a timely and knowledgeable fashion while creating a positive phone call experience for each caller.
  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere to enhance quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider(s)
  • Understand provider to patient flow and anticipate provider’s next steps to the best of their ability
  • Perform inventory responsibilities and stocking of supplies and equipment as requested
  • Attend all in-house training and continued education opportunities

Qualifications:

  • Healthcare Experience is required.
  • Medical Receptionist Experience preferred.
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems preferred.
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills.
  • Must be professional, reliable and dedicated employee.
  • Prefer prior experience working in a dermatology / medical environment preferred. 
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends.

Hourly Pay Range: $17-21

Job Summary: Full-Time Medical Assistant at our Mt Vernon Office. The Medical Assistant is responsible for performing the highest quality of medical, clinical, and clerical tasks in a medical setting. Previous healthcare experience is required.

Medical Assistant

  • Healthcare experience required
  • Nationally Certified Medical Assistant preferred
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook

  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends

Job Summary: Full-Time Licensed Practical Nurse - Allergy at our Toms River Office. The Licensed Practical Nurse - Allergy will provide a high level of general care and education to patients by using their knowledge and skills to promote the goal of The Ultimate Patient Experience. Previous allergy experience preferred.

Schedule: Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am - 7:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Licensed Practical Nurse - Allergy

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere to enhance the quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider(s).
  • Provide general care and education to patients in accordance with OSHA regulations.
  • Administer prescribed medications and treatments, including allergy shots, under the direct or indirect supervision from a provider.
  • Prepare necessary supplies for allergy testing and treatments.
  • Perform lung function testing (FeNO and Spirometry) with and without bronchodilators.
  • Assist in the interpretation of patch testing results and perform placement and removal as directed by an RN or provider.
  • Maintain the immunotherapy room with necessary supplies and materials, ensuring cleanliness.
  • Administer allergy shots and ensuring provider is on site.
  • Observes, records and reports patients’ vitals and reactions to treatments.
  • Assesses patients’ needs and suggest solutions to patient care problems.
  • Supervise triaging of patient communications (through email and/or portal).
  • Maintains accurate patient records, document all visits in EMR.
  • Assures patient stays for required observation time after injections.
  • Learn and perform immunotherapy vial mixing procedures and proper documentation in accordance with current regulations.
  • Reacts appropriately in patient reaction situations, informs physician and/or other clinical staff as necessary to mitigate adverse reactions.
  • Assist providers in recording prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, prescriptions, prior authorization (including biologics), and procedures within established guidelines.
  • Understand provider to patient flow and anticipate provider’s next steps to the best of their ability.
  • Demonstrate clinical competence and sound knowledge base in the provision of quality patient care.
  • Ensure allergy test sets and emergency kits are filled, current, and up to date.
  • Confirm that insurance benefits have been verified prior to the preparation of allergy serums.
  • Regularly interact with physicians, other providers, and staff to identify and resolve problems.
  • Maintain knowledge of trends and developments in the field by reading appropriate articles, journals, and related materials; and by attending seminars and conferences as needed.
  • Report improperly operating medical equipment and instruments to the supervisor.
  • Perform inventory responsibilities, including but not limited to, ordering and stocking of supplies and equipment as requested.

Qualifications

  • Previous Allergy experience preferred.
  • Graduate from an LPN education program approved by the respective state Education Department.
  • Pass the NCLEX-PN examination.
  • Active LPN license in the state working in required.
  • CPR and AED Certifications required.
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems.
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent patient relations and customer service skills.
  • Open availability to work during weekdays.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA & OSHA compliance.

Hourly Pay Range: $25 - $31.50

job.description:
Schweiger is one of the leading dermatology practices in the country with over 580+ healthcare providers and over 170+ offices in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California. Schweiger provides medical, cosmetic, and surgical dermatology and allergy services with over 2.5 million patient visits annually.<br/><br/>Our mission is to create the Ultimate Patient Experience and a great working environment for our providers, support staff and all team members.<br/><br/>Schweiger has been included in the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies in America list for seven consecutive years. Schweiger has also received Great Place to Work certification. To learn more, click here.

Schweiger's Ultimate Employee Experience:  

  • Multiple office locations, find an opportunity near your home

  • Positive work environment with the tools to need to do your job and grow

  • Full time employees (30+ hours per week) are eligible for:

    • Medical (Virtual Care included), HSA/FSA, Dental, Vision on 1st of the month after hire date

    • 401K after 30 days of employment

    • Company Sponsored Short Term Disability (Only applicable for non-California employee)

    • Pre-tax savings available for public transit commuters

    • Your birthday is an additional personal holiday

  • Part-time employees (less than 30 hours) are eligible for:

    • Dental and Vision on 1st of the month after date of hire

    • 401K after 30 days of employment

  • Employee discounts on Schweiger skin care products & cosmetic services 

Position Summary 

We are seeking an experienced Senior HRIS Analyst with deep expertise in the Workday platform to support, optimize, and enhance our global Human Resources systems. This role will serve as a key partner to HR, Payroll, Benefits, IT, and business stakeholders, ensuring Workday solutions are scalable, efficient, and aligned with business objectives. 

The ideal candidate has strong functional and technical knowledge across Workday HCM, Benefits, Payroll, Integrations, Reporting, and Learning (LMS), along with experience leading system enhancements, troubleshooting complex issues, and driving continuous process improvement. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Serve as the primary functional expert for Workday Human Capital Management (HCM).

  • Configure, maintain, and optimize Workday modules, including:

  • Core HCM

  • Benefits Administration

  • Payroll

  • Learning (LMS)

  • Design, build, test, and support Workday integrations using:

  • Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB)

  • Core Connectors

  • Workday Studio (preferred)

  • Web Services/APIs

  • Develop and maintain Workday reports, dashboards, and calculated fields to support HR and business reporting needs.

  • Partner with HR, Payroll, Benefits, Finance, IT, and vendors to gather requirements and implement system enhancements.

  • Support Workday releases by evaluating new features, testing functionality, and coordinating deployment activities.

  • Lead configuration changes, data validation, testing, and production migration.

  • Troubleshoot production issues and provide timely resolution for system defects and integration failures.

  • Ensure data integrity, system security, and compliance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements.

  • Create documentation, standard operating procedures, and end-user training materials.

  • Participate in HR technology roadmap planning and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Qualifications 

  • Bachelor’s degree in HR, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business Administration, or related field.

  • 5–8+ years of HRIS experience.

  • 4+ years of hands-on Workday administration and configuration experience.

  • Strong expertise in:

  • Workday HCM

  • Benefits

  • Payroll

  • Reporting

  • Integrations

  • Learning (LMS)

  • Experience building and supporting Workday integrations using EIB, Core Connectors, and APIs.

  • Advanced knowledge of Workday reporting, calculated fields, and dashboards.

  • Experience supporting Workday releases, testing, and production deployments.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Workday Pro or Workday Certifications in one or more functional areas.

Technical Skills 

  • Workday Core HCM

  • Workday Benefits

  • Workday Payroll

  • Workday Learning (LMS)

  • Workday Reporting

  • Calculated Fields

  • Dashboards

  • Workday Security

  • EIB

  • Core Connectors

  • Workday Studio

  • REST/SOAP APIs

  • XML/XSLT

  • SQL (preferred)

  • Microsoft Excel (Advanced)

Core Competencies 

  • HRIS Strategy and Administration

  • Business Process Configuration

  • Requirements Gathering

  • System Optimization

  • Data Analysis

  • Process Improvement

  • Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Project Management

  • Change Management

  • Customer Service

  • Attention to Detail

Compensation Range: $85,000-$95,000

This remote position is open to candidates located in the following states: New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California

Job Summary: The Laboratory Coordinator is responsible for supporting laboratory operations through specimen intake, administrative duties, data entry, transcription, and general lab maintenance. This role does not involve performing technical laboratory duties but is critical to maintaining the efficiency of lab processes. The Lab Coordinator is expected to adhere to all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) with attention to detail, accuracy, professionalism, and a strong commitment to compliance and safety.

Schedule: Full Time, 30+ hours. Monday to Friday 7:30am – 4:00pm.

Laboratory Coordinator:

  • Receive laboratory specimens from couriers. 
  • Review specimens for proper labeling and acceptability. 
  • Resolve labeling discrepancies according to SOPs. 
  • Sort specimens for in-house processing or send-outs based on insurance coverage, provider preference, and case type. 
  • Accession specimens into the Laboratory Information System (LIS). 
  • Prepare cases for scanning including performing quality control checks. Then scanning specimens into the LIS.
  • Prepare cases for reference laboratories and confirm daily pickups. 
  • Dispose of biohazard and hazardous waste in accordance with policies and regulations. 
  • Maintain a safe and clean work environment, adhering to all OSHA, CLIA, and company-specific protocols. 
  • Lab Coordinator is responsible for assisting in all customer inquiries related to but not limited to: 
  • Assist with inquiries related to: 
  • Missing or delayed pathology reports. 
  • Modifications to orders, requisitions, or reports. 
  • Requests for slides or blocks for consultations and second opinions. 
  • Investigate and resolve lab-related inquiries, including cases processed both internally and at reference laboratories that come in the form of phone calls, voicemail, ModMed/EMA tasks, email and support tickets (via Fresh Desk) 
  • Provide data entry support to Pathologist(s). 
  • The Lab Coordinator will receive diagnostic codes and/or additional test orders from the pathologist.
  • Codes and orders will be shared by the pathologist either verbally or handwritten on pathology requisitions.
  • The Lab Coordinator will enter the orders into the LIS for the other team members to access and process. 
  • The Lab Coordinator will enter the diagnostic code(s) and associated billing code(s) into the LIS to produce a macro, a paragraph of diagnostic information. 
  • The Lab Coordinator will close the case which will add the case to the queue for the pathologist to sign-out.

General Laboratory Duties: 

  •  File and retrieve histology slides and paraffin blocks following laboratory protocols. 
  •  Maintain an organized filing system for easy access and retrieval. 
  •  Assist with archiving and tracking slide and block locations. 
  •  Keep workstations, lab benches, and equipment clean and organized. 
  •  Dispose of biohazard waste properly and restock cleaning supplies. 
  •  Clean and disinfect lab equipment and ensure compliance with safety regulations. 
  •  Maintain inventory, restock lab supplies, and put away shipments upon arrival. 
  •  Assist in audits, quality control (QC), and compliance-related tasks as needed. 

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma/GED minimum required; Associate degree preferred 
  •  Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook with strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills with six months experience in a similar role. 
  • Training and a post training assessment for all role-applicable SOPs and Laboratory Compliance workflows must be completed after hire but before any laboratory work can be completed independently. A competency assessment will occur at one month before independent work is permitted. Role specific SOPs and Laboratory Compliance workflows are outlined in the Pathology Training Program Smartsheet. 
  • Employee is expected to be in their office(s) during the week. Employee may be expected to travel up to 25% or less of their time from their home office. Other travel outside of their region and/or to the corporate office may be needed from time to time.

This role is based in Glen Carbon, IL

Hourly Pay Rate: $14.77 -$18.46

Job Summary: Part-Time Medical Coordinator at our Brea Office. The Medical Coordinator role supports clinical and administrative duties, with a focus on both Medical Assistant and Patient Coordinator functions. This role is responsible for performing the highest quality of clinical and front office responsibilities to support patients and providers. Previous healthcare experience is required.

Schedule: Part time, less than 30 hours per week. Availability Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 8:00am - 5:00pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Medical Coordinator (Medical Assistant/ Patient Coordinator)

  • Patient and Provider Support: Foster a welcoming and professional environment to enhance patient care and support the provider. Maintain a consistent and professional office presence.
  • Clinical Assistance: Assist providers with medical, cosmetic, and laser procedures. Ensure proficiency in all treatments, as well as pre-care and post-care instructions, anticipating provider needs to optimize patient flow.
  • Operational Duties: Prepare and maintain exam rooms before and after procedures. Ensure equipment is in working order and perform daily inventory checks on supplies, including retail and cosmetic products. Alert the team and General Manager of any low supplies as needed.
  • Inventory Management: Oversee the stocking of medical supplies and equipment. Ensure that all supplies are adequately stocked and maintain inventory records as requested.
  • Documentation and Patient Management: Properly document prescribed treatments, medications, lab requisitions, biopsies, cultures, photos, and patient consent forms. Manage follow-up appointments and track inventory used during each visit.
  • Patient Interaction: Take payments, manage patient scheduling, and ensure proper documentation of insurance cards, referrals, and demographic information. Uphold privacy standards, ensuring sensitive information is handled securely, per HIPAA regulations.
  • Financial Responsibilities: Complete daily financial tasks, including accurate cash handling, entering charges and payments, and ensuring cash is properly accounted for at the end of each shift. Handle petty cash and deposit all collected payments securely.
  • Phone and Communication Management: Answer all phone calls promptly, confirm Zocdoc appointments, and make outgoing calls for patient retention. Maintain an organized and neat work area, ensuring patient privacy is preserved.
  • Administrative Duties: Ensure that patient records are created and maintained accurately. Check emails and scan inboxes regularly to address time-sensitive issues. Perform other duties as assigned by supervisors.

Qualifications

  • 6 months to 1 year of experience in a dermatology or medical environment required.
  • Proficiency in EMR systems and patient scheduling tools preferred.
  • High School Diploma or GED required; advanced education is encouraged.
  • Certification as a Medical Assistant is highly encouraged.
  • Must be proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Professional, reliable, and dedicated to maintaining high-quality service standards.
  • Must be familiar with HIPAA and OSHA compliance.
  • Work Environment: This role is primarily office-based, utilizing standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and fax machines.

Hourly Pay Range: $21 - $26

Job Summary: Full-Time Licensed Practical Nurse - Allergy at our Morristown, NJ Office. Schedule:  Full time, 30+ hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7a-7p. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

Licensed Practical Nurse - Allergy

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere to enhance the quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider(s).
  • Provide general care and education to patients in accordance with OSHA regulations.
  • Administer prescribed medications and treatments, including allergy shots, under the direct or indirect supervision from a provider.
  • Prepare necessary supplies for allergy testing and treatments.
  • Perform lung function testing (FeNO and Spirometry) with and without bronchodilators.
  • Assist in the interpretation of patch testing results and perform placement and removal as directed by an RN or provider.

  • Learn and perform immunotherapy vial mixing procedures and proper documentation in accordance with current regulations.
